title: Mathematical Operations
intro: These questions disguise ordinary arithmetic. Symbols are redefined (+ might mean ×), or you must interchange given signs/numbers to make an equation true, or simply apply BODMAS to a messy expression. Nothing here is hard maths — the marks go to whoever substitutes carefully and respects the order of operations. Rewrite the expression with the real operations first, then compute.

items.name: Symbol substitution
items.formula: replace each symbol with its defined operation, then BODMAS

items.name: Sign interchange
items.formula: swap the two named signs everywhere, then evaluate

items.name: Check by options
items.formula: plug option values when faster than solving

topics.name: BODMAS-based Operations
topics.details: Apply the order of operations strictly: brackets first, then orders (powers/roots), then division and multiplication left to right, then addition and subtraction left to right. Insert mental brackets around every × and ÷ before touching + and −.

topics.name: Symbol Substitution
topics.details: You are told what each symbol really means (e.g., 'P means +, Q means −, R means ×'). Rewrite the whole expression with the real operations, then apply BODMAS. Do the substitution in writing first.

topics.name: Interchange of Signs & Numbers
topics.details: You are asked which interchange of two signs (or two numbers) makes a given equation correct, or to evaluate after a stated swap. Apply the swap throughout the equation and check both sides balance under BODMAS.

solved.problem: If + and − are interchanged, find the value of 6 + 2 − 4.
If × and + are interchanged, find the value of 5 × 3 + 2.
If the numbers 4 and 6 are interchanged, find the value of 4 + 2 × 6.
If ÷ and × are interchanged, find the value of 8 ÷ 2 × 4.

topics.name: Balancing Equations
topics.details: You must choose the correct set of signs (from options) to fill blanks so the equation balances. Use estimation: the size of the target tells you whether you need × (big jump) or +/− (small change). Then verify with BODMAS.

shortcuts: Rewrite the expression with real operations in writing before computing.
Bracket every × and ÷ mentally before doing + and −.
With options, plug and test — often faster than solving.
Estimate the target size to decide whether a × is needed.
mistakes: Holding the symbol mapping in your head and mis-substituting.
Applying a swap to only one occurrence of a sign instead of all.
Forgetting division and multiplication share a tier (left to right).
pyq: SSC asks one symbol-substitution and one BODMAS/interchange item per Tier-1 set. Careful rewriting beats clever shortcuts here.
summary: Every operations question is arithmetic in disguise. Substitute the real meaning of each symbol, respect BODMAS (brackets, orders, ÷×, +−), and test swaps or options directly. Write the rewritten expression down before computing to avoid slips.
